CausalChain: BNCT delivers high LET radiation -> BNCT induces dense, localized DNA double-strand breaks in tumor cells -> Tumor cells rely on PARP-mediated repair to resolve DSBs -> PARP inhibition impairs DNA repair mechanisms -> Accumulation of unrepaired DNA damage leads to enhanced tumor cell death
Hypothesis: The concurrent administration of a PARP inhibitor with BNCT will synergistically increase tumor cell killing by preventing the repair of BNCT-induced DNA damage, thereby improving the therapeutic efficacy of BNCT in boron-avid cancers.
Abstract: Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT) has emerged as a targeted treatment modality capable of delivering high linear energy transfer (LET) radiation specifically to tumor cells through the selective uptake of boron compounds. Despite its promising therapeutic potential, resistance mechanisms such as efficient DNA repair in tumor cells can limit treatment efficacy. Here, we propose combining BNCT with poly (ADP ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibition to exploit the dependency of boron‐avid tumor cells on DNA repair pathways. The underlying concept is that BNCT induces localized double-strand breaks (DSBs) with high precision and, when PARP is inhibited, the repair of BNCT-induced DNA damage is blunted, leading to enhanced tumor cell death. This approach has the potential to further improve the therapeutic ratio by amplifying cytotoxicity in tumors while sparing normal tissue. The present hypothesis outlines a testable strategy that merits further investigation in both preclinical models and early-phase clinical trials.
